what_it_does: Modern radio systems need ultra-precise timing to send data cleanly. A phase-locked loop (PLL) is a feedback circuit that locks a local oscillator to a reference signal; imperfect PLLs introduce jitter (random timing wobble) and spurious tones that degrade signal quality. This paper presents a charge-pump PLL—the workhorse of industry—that achieves exceptionally low jitter (15.8 femtoseconds root-mean-square, about one-millionth the flutter of previous designs) and near-zero spurious reference tones at 13 GHz clock speed. It combines three innovations: a phase detector that linearizes the pump's gain, a voltage-controlled oscillator tuned for low phase noise, and a sampling-based filter that sharply attenuates unwanted frequencies without requiring huge capacitors. The dual-path architecture balances noise suppression against lock stability.
